interp.text: IP portfolio at high risk — Urgent review required

IP portfolio in good health — Continue to monitor

van_sign_pos: Net Present Value POSITIVE — the patent creates economic value
van_sign_neg: Net Present Value NEGATIVE — review assumptions or strategy
low_ipscore_text: Prioritise improvement of sections scoring below 50%.
risk_text: Review legal strength, geographical coverage and enforcement capacity.
opp_text: Evaluate licensing agreements and new geographical markets.
npv_positive_text: The patent shows economic value. Consider updating the IP valuation for the balance sheet and for access to financing.
npv_negative_text: Review market assumptions (growth, expected life, sector share) or consider licensing strategies to generate IP revenue without direct production.
solid_portfolio_text: Solid IP portfolio. Maintain monitoring and alignment with the company strategy.

action_plan.A: Strengthen the legal position: expand geographical coverage, complete prior art searches and establish an infringement monitoring process.
action_plan.B: Accelerate technological development: complete production testing, consider reducing time-to-market and analyse differentiation from substitute technologies.
action_plan.C: Strengthen the market strategy: conduct a formal market analysis, assess achievable price premium and identify alternative commercialisation channels.
action_plan.D: Optimise the financial structure: reduce development costs, assess tax incentives (Patent Box, R&D credits) and plan cash flow for renewals.
action_plan.E: Align the IP strategy: integrate the patent into the company strategy, consider licensing agreements and strengthen competitive positioning.

action_plan_fallback: Analyse the key factors and define an action plan.

intro.p: Tool developed by the European Patent Office (EPO). Translates the technical, legal, market and strategic characteristics of a patent into a quantitative score (0–200 points) and an estimate of the Net Present Value (NPV) attributable to the patented technology. Version adapted for an international context, with regulatory, financial and market references updated to 2024–2025.

fin_page.title: Financial Data
fin_page.desc: Enter data from the last approved financial statements for the entire company. Values are used to calculate the Net Present Value (NPV) attributable to the patent.

turnover.label: Total Company Turnover
turnover.help: Total annual company turnover (top-line revenue, equivalent to the Revenue line in P&L). NOT just the patented product — the sector share parameter is used to isolate the relevant business area.

direct.label: Direct Production Costs
direct.help: Raw materials, semi-finished goods, direct labour, production services. For manufacturing SMEs typically 60–75% of turnover. Corresponds to Cost of Goods Sold (COGS).

indirect.label: Indirect Costs (General Overheads)
indirect.help: Rent, utilities, admin/marketing/sales salaries, insurance, general expenses not directly attributable to production. Typically 10–20% of turnover.

depreciation.label: Annual Depreciation
depreciation.help: Annual depreciation charge on plant, machinery and equipment (not land/buildings, not amortisation of intangibles). Source: notes to the financial statements.

deprecPeriod.label: Depreciation Period
deprecPeriod.help: Useful life of production assets in years. Typical values: 5–10 years for modern machinery; 3–5 years for electronics and IT equipment. Use the same assumption as in your accounting policies.

sectorShare.label: Turnover Share in Patent Sector
sectorShare.help: Percentage of company turnover attributable to the specific business area in which the patent operates. Example: if the patented product accounts for €600K out of €1.5M total → enter 40.

discount.label: Discount Rate
discount.help: Rate used to discount future cash flows. For unlisted SMEs: risk-free rate (10Y government bond ≈ 3.5%) + business risk premium (4–7%) + illiquidity premium (1–2%) ≈ 8–12%. Suggested default: 10%.
